name: agentguards-codex-selfhosted
description: LLM security guardrails for OpenAI Codex, for a self-hosted AgentGuards appliance — jailbreak detection, prompt-injection and web-content scanning, data-exfiltration blocking, and destructive-command authorization, enforced entirely by hooks. No bundled MCP server: Codex's .mcp.json cannot point at a per-installation URL, so a shared one would silently talk to AgentGuards' SaaS instead of your appliance. Use agentguards-codex instead if you're on the hosted product.

interface.shortDescription: LLM security guardrails for Codex, for a self-hosted appliance
interface.longDescription: AgentGuards screens what Codex does — every prompt and every shell command — and surfaces anything risky for approval before it runs. Enforcing hooks provide jailbreak and prompt-injection detection, web-content scanning, data-exfiltration blocking, and destructive-command authorization. This variant has no bundled MCP server and requires AGENTGUARDS_URL to be set explicitly, so it never silently talks to AgentGuards' hosted service instead of your own appliance. Fail-closed by default; switch to fail-open with a single environment variable.
